text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Minister of Agriculture Roy Blackbeard is to be replaced by his assistant miniter Ronald Sebego. Moves to make Blackbeard head of the Botswana Meat Commission operations in London have been stopped by the BMC mangement and Blackberd, now the last white minister in the Botswana government, is to be its only white overseas representative, as High Commissioner tk the United Kingdom.

- Drugs worth thousands of pula are being pilfered from the country's government hospitals by staff. The acting director of Botswana's major hospital, the Princess Marina, will not confirm the thefts but has said he cannot rule out such a possibiliy.
- Two Nigerian nationals have been arrested in possession of 488 grams of cocaine. They have been remanded in custody.

- Permanent secretaries in Botswana will now cease to be employed on permanent and pensionable terms, but offered five year contracts with renewal linked to performance. Incumbemts will have the choice of remaining as permanent employees or taking a package and then being considered for a contract.

- Telephone connections in Botswana had increased from 50,000 in April 1995 to 73,000 in May this year, according to Botswana Telecommunications Corporation (BTC) chief executive Olebile Gaborone. More than 100 connection to the Internet had been established by two service providers since the service became available in January this year. He also said BTC had a stong venture partner to help it in a bid for one of two licences to operate cellular telephone networks to be issued later this year, but would not identify the company.
